content.1168f68e-99aa-405a-be40-e127e561f1f0: resolveEmbedWorkerScript in src/services/knowledge/embedding/worker-runtime.ts checks, in order: SEA asset kb/embed-worker.cjs (eval), sibling compiled embed-worker.js (tsc dist), sibling kb-embed-worker.cjs (plain-node run of dist/sea-bundle.cjs), sibling embed-worker.ts bundled on the fly with esbuild (vitest/tsx). The worker resolves no file paths: loadOrtWasmBinary runs on the main thread (SEA asset or installed package) and the bytes go in workerData. apra-fleet kb embed-check --model-dir <folder> prints the origin and dims.
content.176d4504-d6d0-43a4-b77d-453ac54dc154: In src/tools/check-status.ts, fleetStatus checks agents.length === 0 and returns the plain string 'No members registered. Use register_member to add one.' before computing kbHealth. A smoke check of the KB section against a fresh sandboxed server (for example a built SEA binary run with 'run --stdio') therefore never shows 'kb ...' lines. Use kbHealthSummary()/kbHealthCompactLines() in tests, or register a member first.
content.1c6f3afa-f936-4ca5-a1df-e00dc51f24a4: src/services/knowledge/embedding/vector-store.ts: entry_vectors(entry_id, kind, ordinal, model_id, model_revision, dims, text_hash, float16 vec BLOB). Triggers entries_vec_ai/au queue ids into kb_embed_pending; entries_vec_retire/ad delete vectors. embed-queue.ts EmbedQueue.kick() only schedules a setImmediate run; the run checks the embedder state, compares kb_index_meta vec_model_id/vec_model_revision/vec_dims/vec_index_version with the active embedder, claims a rebuild (vec_rebuild_owner + heartbeat in BEGIN IMMEDIATE) on a mismatch, embeds batches and deletes other models' vectors when the queue drains. A fresh KB with no entries records the model identity silently (no rebuild log). SqliteProvider.capture kicks the queue and enqueues code-link resolution and never awaits either. kb-providers.ts kbEmbedderSource() attaches getEmbedder unless APRA_FLEET_KB_EMBED=off.
content.266d51a9-b30a-4d52-bf4c-97f26de518d7: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk McpServer.createToolError(message) keeps only error.message, so custom error fields never reach the client. src/services/tool-registry.ts wrapTool catches an Error whose structuredContent is a plain object and returns {content:[{type:'text', text: err.message}], isError:true, structuredContent} itself; other errors are rethrown unchanged. CodeIntelError (code-intelligence-readiness.ts) uses this for E-CODE-INDEX-NOT-READY retry_after_ms/progress. In-process callers of wrapped handlers (memory-contract roundtrip-harness.mjs, record-fixtures.mjs) therefore see an isError envelope, not a rejection, for such refusals and normalize it back to a thrown refusal.
content.2d11a53b-f992-4a4a-aa83-f3670dc08959: src/services/knowledge/kb-config.ts readKbConfigFromDisk returns tokenSecretName for a token_ref ({{secret.NAME}}) config; kb-providers.ts selectProjectProvider passes {secretName} to HttpKbProvider. Because getKbProviders only re-selects when config.json content changes and a secret update does not touch config.json, the value must be resolved per request: HttpKbProvider.request() calls resolveToken() (lookupServerSecret) each attempt. Missing/expired/unreadable secret throws KbHttpAuthError before any request; HTTP 401 re-reads and retries once, second 401 throws reason rejected. tryFlushQueue breaks (keeps queue) on isConnectionError OR KbHttpAuthError; capture/invalidate enqueue then rethrow err.asQueued(). Literal-token sources keep the old behaviour (plain HTTP_401 error, no retry, no enqueue). rawRequest(token, method, path, body, query, nonJson401IsAuth) now takes the token first; tests reaching the private method should use request(method, path, body). Per-URL last success/last 401 times live in kb-http-auth-state.ts and are read by fleet_status (check-status.ts kbHttpCredentialHealth).
content.2e85c726-b08e-4d07-991d-28a387e4a507: src/services/credential-store.ts saveCredentialFile writes a sibling temp file (credentials.json.<pid>.<random>.tmp, mode 0600, enforceOwnerOnly) and renameWithRetry()s it over credentials.json, retrying up to 10 times with 20ms Atomics.wait on EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY (Windows open-file rename), unlinking the temp on failure. Reverting to fs.writeFileSync in place made about 6-8% of concurrent loadCredentialFile-based lookups in another process fail with 'Unexpected end of JSON input' (writer doing 400 alternating credentialSet calls). Any new writer of credentials.json must keep the temp+rename pattern; a temp file in the data dir can be left behind only if the process dies between write and rename.
content.2eadf404-bb9c-4d9f-b4a6-5a9c5ec21c75: src/services/knowledge/embedding/embedder.ts imports 'onnxruntime-web/wasm' lazily. That entry resolves to ort.wasm.bundle.min.mjs, whose Emscripten glue is inlined, so there is no runtime import() of a sibling .mjs, which a SEA cannot do. The runtime gets the WASM as bytes via env.wasm.wasmBinary, with numThreads 1 because the threaded build spawns workers from a script URL. In the SEA the bytes come from the asset 'onnxruntime-web/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.wasm' (WASM_SEA_ASSET), which scripts/gen-sea-config.mjs adds; in plain Node they are read via require.resolve('onnxruntime-web/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.wasm'). @huggingface/transformers v4 is deliberately not used: its Node entry imports onnxruntime-node, which loads a .node binding at import time, plus sharp. build-sea.mjs's loader {'.node':'empty'} would hide that at build time. tests/knowledge/embedder.test.ts asserts via an esbuild metafile that no .node file, onnxruntime-node or sharp is reachable from embedder.ts.
content.45a64b2d-bf11-4967-8b69-d63e25332825: src/services/knowledge/kb-index.ts: SQL triggers on entries enqueue rowids into kb_index_pending, and only reads drain the queue. search() calls drain(), which calls inTxn(), which runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE when the index is ready and the queue is non-empty. A WAL reader that used to be lock-free therefore needs the write lock. Repro: two SqliteProvider handles on one kb.sqlite; one imports entries; a third connection holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE; the other handle's query throws 'database is locked' after about 5.2 s (busy_timeout 5000). Any change to this read path must keep the drain best-effort, or move indexing to the write path.
content.81df596b-4490-4862-8cef-3ad5ee7c0785: src/tools/check-status.ts kbHealthSummary reads readKbConfigFromDisk once and adds kbHealth.credential (KbHttpCredentialHealth, kind secret|literal) only for provider http. Call times come from src/services/knowledge/kb-http-auth-state.ts, an in-memory Map keyed by the URL with trailing slashes stripped (not by provider instance, because a config change replaces the HttpKbProvider), so they show null/never after a server restart until the first KB call. tokenExpiry decrypts the secret via lookupServerSecret only to run jwtExpiry (exp only); resolves uses lookupServerSecretMeta so expired records are never deleted. kbHttpCredentialHealth is wrapped in safeCredentialHealth, which swallows credential-store errors so the KB section still renders.
content.87f501b6-48cb-462b-b112-1ca0a294dca0: src/tools/kb-query.ts: capMerged(rows, limit) is applied to mergedL1 in both splitQuery (the member mixed-tier path) and the unsplit kbQuery path. The effective limit is the explicit input.limit, or the default (20 normally; 6 slim rows with 3 L2 entries for a MEMBER session that gives no limit). Earlier behaviour let the project and global sides each return up to limit, so l1_results could reach twice the limit. The earlier CONFIRMED KB claim that l1_results can exceed limit is out of date. L2 is now also returned in L1 rank order: ids are looked up, then remapped through a Map.
content.8e76e27c-13eb-40bd-bd9f-65473ee3833b: logLine/logWarn in src/utils/log-helpers.ts both append to the fleet log file under FLEET_DIR/logs and mirror to console.error. tests/knowledge/kb-bible-rich-content.test.ts compares a size:mtime snapshot of FLEET_DIR and <repo>/.fleet before and after each test, so a single log line from a background job started by kb_capture fails it. tests/knowledge/kb-sqlite-stock-and-http-guard.test.ts spies console.error over getKbProviders + capture + query and expects zero calls; asynchronous warnings from earlier tests in the same file can land inside that window. Expected background skips (no code index, no resolver) are therefore recorded in kb_index_meta instead of logged, and background embedding is off in the suite via APRA_FLEET_KB_EMBED=off (tests/setup.ts).
content.9b49976a-e24b-45fb-b25c-6a604cb16be7: entries_kw (FTS5, normalized text via kb-normalize.ts, bm25 weights title5 symbols4 source_files4 recall_cues4 error_signatures4 summary3 content1 tags1) and entries_tri (trigram FTS5 over raw title/symbols/source_files) are not external-content tables. Triggers entries_kw_ai/ad/au (the update trigger fires only on the indexed columns) INSERT OR IGNORE the rowid into kb_index_pending. KbKeywordIndex.search() drains pending rows first when the index is ready. kb_index_meta.kw_version must equal KB_KEYWORD_INDEX_VERSION; a mismatch starts a background chunked rebuild claimed with rebuild_owner/rebuild_heartbeat under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and while it runs reads fall back to the legacy entries_fts if present, else a LIKE scan. Changing normalizer output requires bumping KB_NORMALIZER_VERSION so existing DBs rebuild.
content.a888b84b-d7a0-47ad-9318-2f062770cf2f: tests/ascii-only-gate.test.ts and tests/ascii-only-gate-behaviour.test.ts run scripts/check-ascii-only.mjs against the whole tree. A new test that pastes a tool's literal cross-mark (U+274C) refusal text (e.g. from src/tools/compose-permissions.ts) fails the gate, because new files must have zero non-ASCII characters. Write such markers as JS escapes ('\u274c ...'), the way composeFailureText in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/member-provisioning.mjs matches /^(\u274c|\[FAIL\])/.
content.ab967e3e-4b21-4143-8cf0-6d43065535d9: src/services/knowledge/embedding/embedder.ts: the Embedder state is 'idle' until ensureLoaded() runs, and only embedWith() (embedQuery and embedDocuments) calls it. embed-queue.ts drain() returns 'drained' through finishDrain() before any embedDocuments call when kb_embed_pending is empty. sqlite-provider.ts queryEmbedder() returns null unless state === 'ready', and hybridRows never calls embedQuery otherwise. Result: after a restart over a fully embedded KB, hybrid kb_query has no semantic list until some write queues an entry. Seen in a standalone two-process script: after 5 queries the state was still idle with 0 embed calls. Any query-time use of the embedder needs an explicit non-blocking warm-up.
content.af351ced-8562-477e-8122-1baddba46817: SqliteProvider.query calls hybridRows first. It returns null, and the old keyword path runs unchanged, when there is no error_text, no anchor_files/anchor_symbols and no ready query embedder: the embedder must be in state 'ready' with modelId, revision and an embedQuery method, so a read never waits for a model load. Otherwise it fuses keyword, error (FTS column filter on error_signatures), semantic and anchor lists by RRF k=60 (hybrid-rank.ts), multiplies by trust priors, and re-applies every SQL filter to semantic- and anchor-only ids. QueryOptions.disable_lists (internal only) switches individual lists off; the recall eval and the falsifiability tests use it.
content.c4fb3b10-577e-46a8-8ddb-bde2844b57c7: src/services/credential-store.ts exports lookupServerSecret(name) -> {status:'ok', value, meta} | {status:'missing'} | {status:'expired', expiresAt, meta}, and lookupServerSecretMeta(name), which returns the same statuses without decrypting. Persistent store wins over the session store; allowedMembers is not checked (the caller is the fleet server, not a member command); an expired record is reported as expired and left in place, unlike credentialResolve, which deletes expired records on read. kb_setup (src/tools/kb-setup.ts checkTokenRef) uses the meta variant to refuse missing/expired secrets for provider http.
content.f40ed9c2-9dd5-4b32-a216-db902c79ddb2: src/services/session-roots.ts fetches MCP client roots lazily on the first kb_/code_ call via the tool handler's extra.sendRequest({method:'roots/list'}, ListRootsResultSchema, {timeout}), which sets relatedRequestId so the server->client request is written onto the in-flight tools/call response stream. A server-initiated request outside a request context (e.g. listRoots() from oninitialized) goes to the standalone GET SSE stream in StreamableHTTPServerTransport; if the client has not opened one, the message is dropped and the request only fails at its timeout. Verified end to end with the SDK StreamableHTTPClientTransport in tests/kb-code-scope-roots.test.ts.
content.f8b2695a-bfbf-4a63-93de-5dcfe7d6c374: src/cli/secret.ts: with -y (nonInteractive) the --set path reads all of process.stdin, trims it, and aborts with an error on an empty value; --persist then stores it via credentialSet in this CLI process, which writes credentials.json atomically (temp + rename) so a running fleet server reading it concurrently never sees a partial file. Trimming means CRLF from PowerShell pipelines or a trailing newline from az ... -o tsv is harmless. The documented KB refresher recipe (docs/knowledge-layer.md, Named credentials and refreshers) relies on this; tests/knowledge/kb-named-credential-live-e2e.test.ts drives it with execFileSync input.
